- #49009 (closed): Same generic timeout hiding the port-in-use root cause — the upstream fix may not have fully addressed the multi-user/WSL mirrored scenario you describe.
- #41696 (open): Same stuck-startup symptom from a port already occupied on 127.0.0.1:49374, with the same contender-loop behavior.
- #37718 (open): WSL2 `networkingMode=mirrored` port conflict for the Desktop WSL sidecar — different component but the same shared-loopback collision.

Your issue is more specific than any of these — it focuses on the **machine-global fixed port as root cause for multi-user lockout** and includes a useful warning about the "reuse by port occupancy" anti-pattern — so it may still warrant its own tracking. But linking these in your description (as you've already done for some) will help maintainers triage.

Independently confirmed the bug on a real affected setup (desktop 2.0.14, macOS, custom OpenAI-compatible provider with 11 config-declared models): `GET /api/model` returns all 11 with `enabled: true` and `time.released: 0`, yet a fresh client shows none of them — only previously-selected models keep their persisted `show` override.

Verified this branch locally:

- `bun test` in `packages/app` passes, including the new released=0 case.
- Feeding real `/api/provider` + `/api/model` responses from a dev server through the actual `normalizeProviderList()` and the `visible()` decision chain from `models.tsx` (fresh client, no stored preferences): 11/11 models visible with this branch, 0/11 on `dev` with the same data.

One blocker — `bun run typecheck` in `packages/app` fails on this branch:

```
src/context/global-sync/utils.ts(134,7): error TS2322: Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'.
```

The optional `release_date?: string` lives on the config-side models type (`types.gen.ts` ~L1768), but the assignment target in `normalizeProviderList` uses the catalog model entry type where `release_date: string` is required (~L2110). CI doesn't run typecheck, which is probably why it slipped through. Using `""` instead of `undefined` would keep the one-line fix type-safe — `DateTime.fromISO("")` is also invalid, so the `!date.isValid` escape hatch in `models.tsx` still fires.

Two nits while reviewing: `utils.test.ts` starts with a UTF-8 BOM before the first `import`, and the trailing newline at EOF was dropped.
Up!

Thanks for the triage. Adding context on the linked issues to help with review:

- **#49009** (closed) is the same *symptom* (generic timeout hiding port-in-use) but a single-user macOS scenario — it doesn't cover the root cause tracked here: the fixed machine-global default port combined with per-user service registration.
- **#41696** covers the same stuck-startup / contender loop (already referenced in the description), including the residual contender-overlap gap that still swallows the actionable stderr on 2.0.14.
- **#37718** is a useful data point: it shows the same shared-loopback collision class already bit the Desktop WSL sidecar under `networkingMode=mirrored` (ephemeral port handoff failure instead of a fixed port). Together with this issue, that's a second component affected by the same root cause, which supports treating the fixed default port as the structural problem rather than an environment quirk.

No further action needed from the bot; leaving this open for the root-cause discussion (fixed port + per-user registration, and the warning against fixing it via "reuse by port occupancy").

New metadata from an already authorized native run, not a dedicated reproduction.
Same OpenCode 1.18.23 / Ubuntu 26.04 / `opencode/glm-5.3-flash`, max.
This run includes the local metadata-only fetch observer described above.

Session: `ses_f362f61aaffehYiA8pcxSQnVnS`. All timestamps are 2026-09-22 UTC.

| Milestone | First HTTP request |
|---|---|
| Request start | 15:51:28.437 |
| Headers / status | 15:51:38.488 / HTTP 200 |
| First body bytes | 15:51:38.492 |
| First reasoning event | 15:51:41.097 |
| Stream EOF | 16:21:30.062 |
| Correlation header | `cf-ray: a3f278a4ce3ca9c0-CMH` |

The observer counted 17,016 SSE data frames, but no visible-answer event and no
`[DONE]` frame before EOF. Elapsed request time was 1,801.625 seconds. The native
process then started a second HTTP request at 16:21:32.255; our wrapper did not
restart it or request a continuation. Its headers arrived at 16:21:43.280, HTTP
200, `cf-ray: a3f2a4ad0a05a9c0-CMH`; first reasoning was 16:21:43.282.

At 16:24 UTC the second request was still in progress. There is no terminal usage
receipt for the first request. The wrapper has no total/generation deadline; the
observer's first-byte silence timer was disarmed when body bytes arrived. The host
had over 6 GiB available RAM and low CPU load during the first request.

Can you correlate the two request IDs and check whether any upstream 30-minute
boundary explains the incomplete stream? We cannot establish the cause from
client milestones. This differs from the earlier ten-minute startup delays:
reasoning began promptly, and the failure occurred after the stream had started.
No prompts, customer data, raw SSE payloads or reasoning text are included.

Update: the second request completed with `[DONE]` at 16:30:02.143, after
509.888 seconds; its first visible answer was 16:29:31.394. The native process
exited successfully at 16:30:02.391, 2,320.493 seconds after invocation start.
It emitted one terminal usage record (66,021 reasoning and 5,571 visible output
tokens), while the observer saw two HTTP requests. Our receipt therefore marks
total usage as partial/unknown. No further experimental invocations were started.

I’ve implemented a local version of this behaviour as an OpenCode plugin and have now been using it successfully in normal use.

The basic flow is:

usage_limit_reached → read the provider’s reset timestamp → persist the recovery state → wait locally without model calls → resume the same session after reset.

A few things I’ve found from real-world testing:

* It works with both 5-hour and weekly quota resets.
* Recovery state needs to be persistent rather than an in-memory timer.
* The pending recovery survives OpenCode restarts.
* It has also survived OpenCode being updated while waiting on two separate occasions.
* A single-owner/lock mechanism is useful to prevent duplicate recovery submissions after a restart.
* The model/variant/agent and original session can be preserved when resuming.
* The waiting process itself doesn’t need to make provider/model requests.
* I also added a notification when work actually resumes and when it finishes if longer than 2 minutes.

I’ve been using this in production rather than just testing it synthetically, and automatic recovery has been reliable so far.

If this would be useful for the core implementation, I’m happy to provide more detai.

## Deterministic pixel comparison: `v2` vs this branch

Built a new Drive fixture with 9 dense sessions (mixed thought/tool messages, groups spanning messages, tools between groups, failures inside groups, 18-tool exploration runs, 9-thought runs, generic/web/execute tools, notices + compaction, and a 14-turn history that exercises tail-first backfill). Both builds run the identical script; the only variable is the checkout.

| Profile | Frames | Identical |
|---|---|---|
| Grouped, thinking hidden — 3 widths × top/bottom + sequential disclosure clicks | 88 | **88** |
| Ungrouped, thinking shown — 3 widths × top/bottom | 54 | **54** |

**142/142 pixel-identical.** Full RGBA comparison, no masks or tolerances.

Two earlier runs showed divergent frames in the two longest sessions; investigating each showed same content at a different scroll offset — the harness's "settled" check was passing mid-backfill after `ctrl+g`. Tightened the harness to pin the session title to the top before every click. No code change was needed; the divergence did not reproduce once the harness was deterministic.

Added `session-backfill-disclosure.test.tsx` to lock in the one scenario the earlier matrix never combined: clicking a thought group that was mounted by backfill.

Full TUI suite on the rebased branch: 1367 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail. Typecheck passes.

## Still reproducible in v2.0.12 (stable) — different trigger conditions

Confirmed the **same root cause** as the original report but with a different trigger path that does **not** match the original 4-condition checklist (no `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, no `oh-my-openagent`).

### Environment

- **OpenCode version**: v2.0.12 (stable, current)
- **OS**: Arch Linux (rolling, kernel Zen)
- **Terminal**: opencode TUI (no external terminal)
- **Env flag set**: `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true` (note: different flag — *not* the parent `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` documented in the original report)
- **Plugins loaded**:
  ```
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman/caveman-config.cjs
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman/package.json
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/telemetry-runtime.ts
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/model-variants.ts
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-review-transport.ts
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/sdd-task-result-artifacts.ts
  ~/.config/opencode/plugins/skill-registry.ts
  ```

### Trigger

Native `question` tool with `questions` array containing **3 entries** (SDD preflight canonical pattern: Pace / Artifacts / PR strategy, each with 2-3 options, header ≤ 30 chars, all valid JSON). Reproduced 5+ times across varied payloads (with/without `multiple` field, varied header text, varied option lengths, English-only and Spanish-localized text). All attempts fail with the same error:

```
{"error":{"type":"unknown","message":"Attempted to assign to readonly property."},"content":[]}
```

### Evidence

1. `question` tool with **1 entry** → first attempt errored with `SDD preflight refused: ask Pace, Artifacts, and PR strategy in ONE ` + "exactly three questions"` confirming the SDD preflight contract requires 3 questions.
2. `question` tool with **3 entries** → error `readonly property` reproducible with every payload variation.
3. Same `question` tool invocation succeeds when issued from chat text instead (no native tool), confirming the bug is in the native tool dispatcher, not in the orchestrator.

### Likely root cause

Per original report: Immer `produce()` freezing the tool input object via `Object.freeze()` after `SyncEvent.run`. The proposed fix in **PR #25867 (`input: structuredClone(value.input)`)** was never merged (auto-closed as stale on Jun 5, 2026 by `automated-pr-cleanup`).

The current trigger path is *not* the same as the original (no `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, no `oh-my-openagent`), which suggests the v2 event system may have a *broader* activation surface than the four conditions in the original bug — possibly any plugin that hooks `tool.execute.before`, or any tool call where the event bus reaches `SyncEvent.run` regardless of the parent experimental flag.

### Request

1. **Reopen this issue** — the bug is reproducible in current stable.
2. **Reopen PR #25867** or extract the `structuredClone` fix into a focused PR.
3. If the trigger surface is broader than documented, update the original 4-condition checklist in the bug report.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```js
// From any OpenCode agent session with the env + plugins listed above:
question({
  questions: [
    { question: "Pace?", header: "Pace", options: [...] },
    { question: "Artifacts?", header: "Artifacts", options: [...] },
    { question: "PR strategy?", header: "PR strategy", options: [...] }
  ]
})
// → { error: { type: "unknown", message: "Attempted to assign to readonly property." } }
```

The single-question equivalent of the same call pattern succeeds in the SDD preflight tool, which confirms the per-entry schema is valid and the failure is in the multi-entry dispatch path.

Additional data on this same crash from the 1.18.31 builds (2026-09-19 onward): it is a regression in 1.18.31 and the SIGILL is deterministic at one absolute instruction address across independent processes.

Verified against the shipped `opencode` 1.18.31 binary (ET_EXEC, non-PIE, base `0x200000`):

- `opencode[7722]`: ILL_ILLOPN (ud2) at `ip:2607064`
- `Worker[65104]` (second, unrelated process): ILL_ILLOPN (ud2) at `ip:2607064`

`ip:2607064 - 0x200000 = opencode+0x2407064`, byte-identical to this issue's documented ud2 site in OpenTUI's `drawTextBuffer`. With a fixed (non-PIE) base the same absolute RIP is expected; the noteworthy part is that >=14 such ILL_ILLOPN traps have landed since 2026-09-19 (several/hour at peak) across several independent install paths, and every one reports `coredumpctl: missing` - the SIGILL cores are silently dropped, so the only physical core from the whole run is a concurrent int3 halt in a third process (PID 71263, 157,990,957 B zst; happy to upload it if useful).

OOM is ruled out (31 GiB RAM / 62 GiB swap never under pressure). The crash-time dlopened modules `/tmp/libopentui.so` and the `fff` Rust cdylib carry no GNU build-id, which blocks symbolization of library-local frames.

A second already-authorized native invocation reproduced an approximately 30-minute stream failure. No new dedicated reproduction was launched. Same OpenCode1.18.23, Ubuntu26.04, `opencode/glm-5.3-flash`, max, and the same local metadata-only observer.

Session: `ses_f35d99b2affekLdKPJWJ3pedTL`. Times below are 2026-09-22 UTC.

| Milestone | First HTTP request |
|---|---|
| Request start |17:25:09.774|
| Headers / status |17:25:19.672 / HTTP200|
| First reasoning |17:25:20.162|
| Reader failure (`stream_error`) |17:55:11.283|
| Correlation header |`cf-ray: a3f301e2483f9934-JAX`|

The observer counted21,890 SSE data frames. No visible-answer event or terminal `[DONE]` was recorded. Elapsed request time was1,801.509s. The prior occurrence ended after1,801.625s, although that observer outcome was clean EOF rather than a reader failure. This similarity suggests a boundary worth investigating; it does not establish which component imposed it.

The native process then began HTTP request2 at17:55:13.759. Headers arrived17:55:26.356, HTTP200, `cf-ray: a3f32decb94c665a-PHL`; first reasoning17:55:28.943. It was still running at17:56UTC. Our wrapper did not restart the native process or ask for a continuation and has no generation timeout. Its first-byte silence timer had disarmed when the first body bytes arrived.

The 20MiB `MAX_MEDIA_INGEST_BYTES` ingest cap that landed bounds peak memory for oversized files but does not stop image bloat below that size. The architectural fix is tracked in #46173 (managed per-session attachment store, currently open).

Image-specific angle (previously #49320, closed as duplicate): the `read` tool persists the full `data:<mime>;base64,...` URI in `session_message` tool-result records — verified on v2.0.14 (1,259,239 chars for a single PNG in this reporter's DB). `boundImages` (packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts) also sums `Buffer.byteLength(uri)` for these file parts, so image payloads are counted twice (~2x context/usage). The new 20MiB `MAX_MEDIA_INGEST_BYTES` read-side cap mitigates the OOM side of this issue but leaves everything under 20MB unchanged. The managed per-session attachment store in #46173 should be the real fix.

Adding current evidence for the third-party OpenAI-compatible client path, plus one gap that the earlier fix does not cover.

Reproduction as of today:

- Provider `opencode-go`, model `mimo-v2.5`, base URL `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`
- Client: Hermes Agent (plain OpenAI-compatible chat completions)
- A tool result that carries an image is sent as multi-part content on `role: "tool"`:
  `[{"type":"text","text":"..."},{"type":"image_url","image_url":{...}}]`
- Xiaomi rejects the request: 400, `param: "text" is not set`

The part worth flagging: the transform in #32966 only handles **single-part** tool results. It flattens a lone text/error part to a string and explicitly leaves multi-part content as an array. Multi-part is exactly the shape this bug is about, so even with that transform merged, a tool result carrying an image would still 400.

What would actually close it for these providers, either way:

- hoist media out of the tool result into a normal user message — this is the existing behavior for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` in the CLI (`supportsMediaInToolResult` returns false for it, so the image is extracted and re-injected as a user message), and it is the same approach PR #50272 just merged for Bedrock; or
- for `role: "tool"` messages specifically, emit plain-string content and move the media part to an adjacent user message.

Worth noting the asymmetry: the opencode CLI itself does not hit this, because it already hoists media out of tool results for OpenAI-compatible SDKs. It only bites clients that talk to `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` directly and treat "OpenAI-compatible" literally. Since Go is advertised as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, closing that gap on the relay side would fix every third-party client at once instead of each one shipping its own workaround.

Happy to test a fix or provide a minimal request payload if useful.

Update: found a workaround.

In the providers UI I disabled the `Personal / OpenCode` group, clicked around, then re-enabled it — after that the `Polza` group appeared in `/models` and the custom models became selectable.

So the data was always there (server-side `model.list` returned all 22 `polza/*` models with `enabled: true` all along); the `/models` dialog just never refreshed its list — not on config hot-reload (`provider.updated` events fire, I verified in `opencode.log`), not on app restart, OS reboot, or Electron cache purge. Toggling an unrelated provider forced the refresh.

Looks like the dialog caches the model list on first open and doesn't invalidate it when providers/models update.

Additional confirmation on Linux with the latest stable OpenCode release.

I upgraded OpenCode from `1.18.10` to `1.18.32` and ran:

```sh
opencode --pure models openai --refresh --verbose
```

The GPT-5.6 native OpenAI entries still resolve to:

```text
context: 400000
input:   272000
output:  128000
```

This affects `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-luna-fast`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-sol-fast`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-terra-fast`. The `max` variant is present, but it only sets `reasoningEffort: "max"`; it does not change the model limit.

For comparison, the same command reports `1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000` for `gpt-5.4`, while the official GPT-5.6 model cards report the same `1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000` envelope:

- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna

A user `provider.openai.models.<model>.limit` override changes the reported metadata, so this appears to be a stale/hardcoded OAuth/catalog clamp rather than an API capability limitation.
